answer.summary: Teen Accounts are meant to give teens an age-appropriate, safer Instagram experience and address parents’ concerns. Teens are placed in the safest settings by default, including private accounts; under-16s need parental permission to change defaults, and existing public accounts move to private unless parents permit them to stay public.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.content: Gleit described Teen Accounts as putting teens into the safest settings by default and creating an age-appropriate experience. The launch was focused on parents’ biggest concerns about teens on social media; it simplified and standardized existing features and added functionality for parental control. Gleit said parents’ knowledge of their own children was the initiative’s north star.

sections.heading: How the defaults work
sections.content: All teens are put into the safest settings, with a private account as one default. Under-16s need their parents’ permission to change any of these defaults. As a result, teens who already had public accounts are automatically moved to private unless they get parental permission to remain public.
